purpose: Composite speech and character texture drawn from interview patterns without using direct transcript language.
strict_rule: Do not quote, paraphrase too closely, or attribute interview language. Treat these as newly written composite patterns.
shared_speech_patterns: Answer from the season, task, terrain, or labor calendar before abstract principle.
Move from values to work sequence: who checks cattle, who fixes fence, who watches calves, who pays, who gets called when something breaks.
Use stories as evidence, but make them generic or composite: fire, hard winter, failed fence, bad bull, weak signal, neighbor's failed technology.
Let contradiction remain visible: a character can dislike a tool and still use it.
Do not use consultant language when an operator phrase will do.
operator_details_to_seed: Two-person operations make small new chores decisive.
Family and neighbors may help at branding/weaning but not on ordinary weeks.
Labor scarcity is also skill scarcity: roping, horsemanship, low-stress handling, equipment repair, judgment.
Aging bodies change what practices are sustainable.
Later calving can reduce weather loss and night-check stress but requires a different marketing strategy.
Records and sensors only matter if someone uses the information to change decisions.
Social media is necessary for market access and dangerous for trust.
Direct-market truth matters because unverifiable claims can earn premiums without the cost of doing the work.
Imported or high-status genetics can fail if they do not fit place, temperament, climate, or handling realities.
composite_voice_examples: That depends on what month you are asking about.
Show me where the hours leave the week.
A sensor that creates three chores and removes one did not save labor.
If the audit stops at the farm gate, it is not much of an audit.
Do not call it stewardship until you can show what changed for the animal or the ground.
